turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Diario Humano reports Los Cabos residents begin a signature drive on the 19th under the slogan 'The Coastal Road stays!'

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. They want the East Cape route kept in the 2040 urban plan as a rustic road.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The 2025 update would have dropped 3.9 km of that route.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Really? That seems like a small slice, yet it changes everything for the coast. [pause] I keep picturing the long stretch where the desert meets the water.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The full stretch runs 94 km from San José del Cabo to La Ribera.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Grupo Questro offered an alternative highway at least one kilometre inland instead.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Implan suggests keeping it as a scenic drive with beach access.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Ha, of course. The mayor says any choice will go to public consultation first.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Residents collect signatures through the 22nd to make sure the road stays.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does it mean for a road to belong to the coast rather than simply cross it?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: This is Radio BCS2050.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Today's deep dive on Urbanism, and the question we chase is how a city learns where the road should end and the desert begin.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Governor Víctor Castro just handed over 50 property titles in Los Frailes, Santa Rosalía, plus nine starter homes across the municipality.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: HCN reports the delivery came with 6.4 million pesos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The state housing institute has now reached 992 actions in Mulegé over five years.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That total reaches 145.4 million pesos. [pause] Families who once held no papers finally hold something solid.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes for a family the day the title arrives?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The governor's delivery included 50 property titles in Los Frailes and nine homes across the towns.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. The desert teaches patience, but a title speeds things up for the next generation.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Los Cabos residents are collecting signatures this week to keep the East Cape Coastal Road inside the 2040 plan.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Diario Humano says the slogan is simple: “The Coastal Road stays!”

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They want the 94-kilometre route preserved as a rustic scenic drive rather than removed.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The 2025 update would have dropped 3.9 kilometres. [chuckle] That stretch matters to people who walk it every day.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: A developer offered an alternative highway one kilometre inland. The mayor says any choice goes to public consultation.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Really? What would you ask the families who live right on that coast?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The signature drive runs from the 19 to the 22 of November.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: People will stand in line with the sea breeze behind them.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: I keep thinking about the quiet mornings when the light hits the water and the road still feels like theirs.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Meganoticias reports the first 704 homes in Sierra Vista are over 90 percent built.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: These units will move families out of stream beds and informal settlements in Los Cabos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: More than 17,000 homes have already been assigned under the same programme.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The mayor points to land and drinking water as the remaining hurdles. [pause] One project agreed with Infonavit in San José del Cabo.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: How long does a family wait once the keys are almost ready?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Land and drinking water remain the biggest obstacles for the mayor.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: How does the city stretch when water lines run short?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The homes measure 44 square metres each. That small space can hold an entire new start.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. And the signatures run from the 19 to the 22. People will line up with pens and hope.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Foro Mar de Cortés and the Citizen Observers Network signed an agreement at the 2026 Summit.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: They will create a Sea of Cortez Citizen Observatory and a traffic-light index for biodiversity and illegal fishing.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The traffic-light index will cover biodiversity and illegal fishing.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Ordinary citizens watching the water could change how decisions are made.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Semarnat’s BCS head witnessed the signing. The goal is an annual report and early-warning network around the entire Gulf.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does it mean when ordinary citizens become the first eyes on the water?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: I keep picturing the long road south, dust on the tires, the light hitting the water.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: These stories all circle the same question. [breath] How does a desert coast decide who belongs where, and on what terms?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mulegé sits sparse along the northern corridor, where the desert meets the sea in long empty stretches.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Los Cabos holds 351111 people and drives the south with its airport and hotels.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does daily life feel like out in those northern towns when services stay so thin?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: HCN reports Governor Víctor Castro Cosío just handed out 59 housing actions in Mulegé last week.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: 50 of those were property titles in Los Frailes, Santa Rosalía.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Really? That must shift something for families who have lived without clear ownership.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The other nine were small starter homes, each 44 square metres.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Spread across Santa Rosalía, Guerrero Negro and Heroica Mulegé. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: 6.4 million pesos for that single day.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Over five years the state housing institute has counted 992 actions in the municipality.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Worth 145.4 million pesos total.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: I keep wondering what those titles change for a family living far from any market.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Down south, Diario Humano says residents in Los Cabos are gathering signatures this week to keep the East Cape Coastal Road.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Nineteen to 22 November, under the slogan The Coastal Road stays.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The 2025 plan update would have dropped 3.9 kilometres from the route.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: From the full 94-kilometre stretch between San José del Cabo and La Ribera.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Grupo Questro wants a highway at least one kilometre inland instead.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Implan prefers a scenic drive with beach access, and the mayor says any choice goes to public consultation.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Wait—what would you ask the families who just received those titles in Los Frailes?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: How the new road plan might shape the daily walk to the water for people along the East Cape.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep thinking about the quiet mornings out there, where the light stretches across empty land and a title finally makes a house feel like home.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mm. The desert teaches patience with distance, yet the city keeps stretching anyway. [pause]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would you ask the planners who still hold that 2040 map open?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: How the light on that long road south still feels wide open. [laugh]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The new bus route to El Centenario and Chametla keeps coming up in the news.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: HOY BCS notes the council used reallocated Ramo 33 funds for two buses, following the earlier Pedregal–Centro line.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It feels like a small fix for a bigger pattern.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. The portal's earlier Foresight already flagged water and port questions reopening the whole territorial debate in Cabos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And now the summit in Los Cabos is bringing leaders together under that same heading of cities and climate.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Tus Buenas Noticias says the Foro Mar de Cortés runs through 10–12 November, with sessions on regional competitiveness and limits to development.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Limits feel like the quiet thread here.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meganoticias reported the private sector asking for density caps and protection of the East Cape coastal road.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Because the 2025 plan update was never published.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Right. So the process restarted without final approval.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. What does that do to the long-term map?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Base de datos BCS 2050 shows Los Cabos still constrained by water scarcity.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the 0317/0319 rules sit on top of that.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meanwhile La Paz just decided against new borrowing for December payroll.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Really? Palabra BCS says they moved the MXN 71.5m year-end bonus forward.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Using own revenue and early property-tax payments.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: One number at a time, yet the same pressure sits underneath both places.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The knowledge graph lists La Paz revenue, still tied to the same water–energy coupling.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And then the tides reach homes that used to stay dry.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meganoticias covered the flooding in Puerto San Carlos and El Dátil, with over 300 homes under water after the berm failed.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Governor Castro links it straight to climate change already arriving on the coast.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal's Foresight called this coastal resilience joining the 2050 ceiling, right alongside the earlier hurricanes.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: But here's the thing that surprised me.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The resurfacing of Bulevar 5 de Febrero started after the rainy-season damage.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Diario Humano reports just a 3.3 million peso job.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: A single road repair suddenly feels like the visible edge of everything we just traced. [pause]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. The hidden thread runs from the buses and the bonus straight through the plans that never got published.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And it still has to hold when the next high tide comes. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Did you know the state just set a target of 37,500 housing actions over six years?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: From the convenio signed in October 2024, yes. [pause] That is one home if they hit the pace.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Exactly. What does that look like on the ground?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It means new streets, new pipes, new wells maybe, all at once.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Yet 22 of 39 aquifers already run in deficit, according to CONAGUA data from 2023.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That is the quiet part nobody puts on the sales brochure.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The annual deficit sums to 105.1 cubic hectometers.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So the desert sets the real pace, not the plans.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: In Comondú the head town of Ciudad Constitución had 43805 residents according to the census from 2020.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The high tide on 25 October pushed water into streets homes schools and the seafront at El Centenario.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So every new house carries the same question the desert always asks.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: How much water is left once the pipes reach the last street?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Last year they financed almost 8993 actions with 6560 million pesos.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Still a long way from the six-year goal.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the population sits at 798447 from the 2020 census.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So the numbers keep climbing while the aquifers keep dropping.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The plans for Los Cabos and La Paz both stay on the books, one from 2013, the other from 2018.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Paper holds the line until the water does not.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep thinking how those neighborhoods look when the water sits there after the sea pulls back.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Whether the housing convenio includes any line for storm barriers or just the pipes and streets now.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Storms keep testing those lines too.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Really? Like the high tide that pushed water into streets and homes in La Paz last October.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. What would you ask the person signing the next convenio?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Whether the desert gets a seat at the table before the concrete does. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep thinking about the streets after a storm in La Paz, water sitting where the plans never quite reached.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The light changes everything then, doesn't it?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It does. What would you ask them about the next set of pipes?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Whether the sea still has room once the last house is tied in. [laugh]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What object in a new home here actually carries the whole planning system inside it?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: I keep coming back to the kitchen faucet. Turn it on and you meet the viability package.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The faucet itself stays quiet about where the water comes from or who signed off.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. Behind every new connection sits the full check: water from DMA and desal, energy through SIBCS, instruments like POERBCS.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: UN-Habitat wrote the International Guidelines on Urban and Territorial Planning in 2015 with twelve principles.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Their 2018 handbook then shows how to run that process at the territorial scale we actually live in.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the faucet also touches the land-use rules in POERBCS and its 56 UGAs.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Wait—those 56 units guide every change of soil use before the water even reaches the tap.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the risks list: aquifer limits, marine intrusion, the isolated grid, ANP boundaries.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The desert light makes those limits feel close, doesn't it? [pause]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The OECD looked at metropolitan growth in 2015 and flagged how corridors like La Paz and Los Cabos behave.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Los Cabos revenue share for 2025 sits at 1,282,611,261 pesos, which funds part of that same pipe network.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: La Paz holds 837,464,432. The faucet therefore depends on those municipal lines as much as on the desal plant.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Really? Those two numbers already show how tightly the budgets lock into the water flow.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: SEPUIMM keeps the infrastructure and energy table that decides whether the connection is even possible.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: One everyday tap therefore links the UN guidelines, the state instruments, and the budget numbers.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The hidden design is that the water only flows after every layer has said yes.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: I keep thinking about the families who sit at those tables before any permit moves forward.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does the desert teach us when we finally see those layers? [chuckle]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It teaches patience, I think. The tap waits for the whole system to align.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. And the swell of the next wave still reaches the shore regardless.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal’s Vision on housing for 2050 keeps coming back to one line: services first, risk second, and water and energy margins that actually exist.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. So not just more houses, but houses that can be served.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. The risk they flag is growth in places without services or right on the coast and over stressed aquifers.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the state had 798,447 people in the 2020 census. That number already feels tight when you picture where the next houses might land.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The aspiration is housing that sits off the first line of risk and stays inside real water and energy limits. No big 2050 unit target is published yet.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would it take to hold that line across the whole peninsula?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The Tendencia 2050 reading says Baja California Sur does not hold together as one repeated coastal formula. It points instead to a polycentric system.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A system of distinct roles rather than one big model stretched end to end.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Los Cabos keeps the tourism engine but carries the water and power stress. East Cape stays in tension with protected areas. Todos Santos and El Pescadero form the Pacific amenity spine.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Then La Paz as the service capital and water-energy node.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Loreto as tourism-conservation anchor. Comondú as agricultural hub with a bit more room. And northern Mulegé as a thinner corridor now seeing a remote generation tender.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That spread feels more honest to the desert and the coast than trying to copy one success everywhere. [pause]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The levers are simple on paper. First relocate what is already exposed before opening new fronts on the coast or on aquifers already in deficit.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And cross-check every proposal against the demand-supply board and the current plans.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Treat the backlog and missing services as a hard ceiling, not something the market will fix later.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The conditions for that future are just as clear: each place keeps its own vocation instead of becoming a diluted version of Los Cabos.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: New growth only where water and energy show real margin or a non-DMA source like desal, without pretending NOM-011 credit.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: East Cape and Loreto would have to respect ANP and POEL ceilings first.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And Comondú and the north add production or energy without draining services or protected zones.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The watchlist starts with the 2027 budget package at 28.3 billion pesos, due for approval in December.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Also the El Tezal partial plan consultation and the Los Cabos urban plan update with its density limits and the Cabo del Este coastal road question.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Housing for Wellbeing sites will need to be checked against actual water and service capacity.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: If those checks hold, the polycentric shape could still be real by 2050.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And if they slip, the single coastal formula comes back fast. [breath]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I keep wondering what it means for a city to actually fit this coast.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Like it was invited to stay rather than told to arrive.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Exactly. Not pushing against the desert or the sea, but letting them set the pace.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mm. The way a home might sit so the morning light still reaches the kitchen table.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the water still finds its way through. I keep thinking about that balance.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What if that became the quiet measure of every new street? [pause]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Then the city would feel less like something added and more like something that already belonged.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: I like that image. It feels hopeful, even when the details are hard.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Exactly. When the city respects where the water wants to flow and where the desert can breathe, everything else seems to fall into place more naturally over time.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Ha, of course. The land has its own memory of where things should go. [chuckle]
